I had taken one of my dogs to this clinic in the past, so I thought it would be a good place to bring my other dog when he developed a severe cough. I called first thing in the morning when they opened. The receptionist told me they had a morning appointment available, so I scheduled it.

Later, right before my appointment (thankfully before I had driven all the way there), someone named Daisha called to tell me the veterinarian wouldn’t be in until 2:00 PM. Since it was a Sunday and there weren’t many veterinary clinics open, I felt like I had no choice but to accept the later appointment. After I agreed to 2:00 PM, she started talking to someone in the background and then said, “Never mind, bring him in at 5:30 PM instead.” This was incredibly frustrating, but again, because of the circumstances, I agreed.

I started asking her a question, she abruptly hung up on me. It was rude and unprofessional. Fortunately, I was able to find another veterinary hospital that could see my dog much sooner. Given the medical issue he was experiencing, it was important that he be examined as soon as possible. I emailed this clinic to let them know I would not be making the 5:30 PM appointment because I was at the other veterinary hospital, where it was too busy and noisy to call. I never even received a confirmation that my cancellation email had been received. The entire experience was disappointing. Because of the disorganized scheduling, poor communication, and unprofessional behavior from the front desk staff, this clinic has lost a customer.

Mixed bag here, there are positives and negatives, the negatives are easily fixed and I'll update the review if I no longer run into those issues. I want to say it's a 4 for anyone who doesn't use pet insurance. 3 stars if you do use it.

The positives:

Great Vets
Quick Appointments and follow-ups
Open 7 days a week and open late
Takes the time to answer your questions even though I'm sure it annoys them.
Trupanion Direct Pay Partner
Accepts many payment methods
Willing to work with your needs as a client

The negatives:

Communication with the Vet - A mixed bag here, as I said before, 4 stars if you don't use insurance. My experience so far shows that there is a constant disconnect in communication between what the vet says and what the vet techs say. Recommendations that the vet made were not clearly expressed to us as clients, and ended up being negatives on the vet notes when used for insurance purposes.

Inconsistent documentation - Every single time I've been here, there have been errors on the vet notes. What the vet techs are writing is not what the actual vets are saying. My biggest gripe has been dental, multiple times listed as no dental disease, and then the paperwork says both stage 1 and no dental disease. It's conflicting information and unfortunately, my pup at the time was within the waiting period, which made dental disease an exclusion with Trupanion.

Honestly its a good vet office, but I think an improvement would be having the actual vet write the vet notes so there are no errors, and do not allow the vet techs to make diagnosis on teeth and other issues. It has messed up my insurance and has issues that aren't pre-existing being listed as pre-existing. Another improvement would be the vet comes and talks to clients about their recommendations for follow ups and testing so their aren't breakdowns in communication.

Overall 3/5 if you use insurance.
4/5 if you don't.
5/5 if those 2 main negatives were addressed.

Price is reasonable. The people are kind.

Edit: My service has gotten much better and I would recommend them!

But to make matters worse, on our return to the U.S. my dogs were denied entry because the paperwork was incomplete.

From the start, communication and professionalism were an issue. I was quoted $351 by email by Jacqueline, but when I went to pay they attempted to charge me over $460.
Despite me showing email proof of the agreed price, the front desk told me I had to pay the higher amount regardless and said only Jacqueline could honor the quoted price.
They claimed Jacqueline was not in the office and therefore they couldn’t do anything about it but I had to pay that amount. After insisting on speaking with someone to resolve it, Jacqueline finally came out and honored the price she quoted.
Which only confirmed they were lying about her presence and tried to make me pay a higher amount than what was agreed.

To make matters worse, my husband called the clinic from the airport when our dogs were denied re-entry to the U.S. due to incomplete paperwork. He was told Jacqueline “no longer worked there,” and couldn’t do anything about the situation.
My husband asked to speak to a manager but they said no manager was available. Which we then asked for a call but that never happened.
Multiple refund requests and emails were ignored, and we ultimately had to file a dispute with our bank, which thankfully was approved since we had to pay again in Mexico for the international health certificates.

This clinic showed dishonesty, lack of accountability, and extremely poor communication, and caused us serious stress and travel complications. Do not recommend this clinic at all.

We went there based on the suggestion and sure enough, the process was successful.  The vet worked with the emergency clinic to send over the X-rays and labs.  Surgery would have been nearly $8,000.  The scope version was $3000.  My sister (who was traveling) saved $5000 and there was little to no recovery time for the dog versus having surgery.  More notably was that this vet did not make the money for the procedure but put the animals needs ahead of paying his own bills.  This is the most ethical and noble of gestures.

The vet was gentle with the dog and was very patient and attentive with my mother (who was caring for the dog).

If we lived in San Antonio, they would definitely have earned our future business.

Do not recommend this clinic! Unprofessional management and education regarding medication  is lacking. Brought my dog into clinic for suspicious twitches, I was told he may have had a focal seizure and the recommended medication was Keppra. Keppra would need to be given every 8 hours but I told the doctor (Jay Meyer) and vet tech (Kristy) I would not be able to stick to this dosing schedule because of my work schedule, so I was told to “just give him the medication whenever you can”. When I was handed the prescription it did not come with any instructions. No medication description, no possible side effects, no signs/symptoms to look out for. NOTHING! So, I started googling the medication and found out that Keppra needs to be given on a STRICT schedule, you can’t just give this medication “whenever” because it can cause worse seizures. I called the clinic to discuss this situation, Raven answered the phone and I expressed my concerns to her and she confirmed the medication couldn’t just be given “whenever” and to go back into the clinic to return the incorrect prescription and receive the correct one. When I arrived to the clinic to return the medication, I was told I wouldn’t be given a refund and after explaining that I deserve the refund since this entire situation could have been avoided if the Dr & tech would have listened to my concerns the first time, BEFORE they prescribed the medication, this wouldn’t have happened. Eventually after a lot of back & forth between the receptionist, Raven & whoever she was talking to in the back, I was told that I WOULD  be receiving the refund. It’s now two weeks later, I have called multiple times and spoke with Raven regarding the refund and still have no update/answer.
